The Qader family of missiles utilizes liquid fuel; the clip likely depicts the fueling process using Red Fuming Nitric Acid (RFNA)—a highly reactive and toxic liquid oxidizer—carried out within the tunnels of Iran's "missile cities." 🇹🇷🇮🇱 Are Turkey and Israel on collision course across the Mediterranean, Black and Arabian Seas?
Israel and Turkey are not just trading barbs following the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) strike on an abandoned Syrian air base — the geography of their confrontation is expanding, reaching into the seas and surrounding regions.
👉 The rise in tensions followed Israel's attack on the Abu al-Duhur military airbase in northwestern Syria's Idlib province on August 18. Days later, Israel's Kan News reported that Israeli security officials had informed the US that Turkey was preparing to deploy a radar system at the airfield which could have shifted the regional balance of power.
Amid the diplomatic war of words, Turkey has moved into northern Syria — despite Israel's warning against moving its troops south. Turkish forces entered Deir ez-Zor on August 29 to build a temporary bridge across the Euphrates alongside Syrian troops, while Turkish drones provided aerial security, a source told the Middle East Eye.
🚢 Meanwhile, the Israeli Navy claimed growing preparations by the Turkish Navy in recent months, including military exercises and an increased naval presence in the Mediterranean and in areas where the Israeli Navy operates, Israel's Channel 11 News reported on August 30. Israeli naval officials view the preparations as a possible sign of a strategic shift, underscoring the need for operational readiness in case of a military confrontation.
Turkey's presence in the Eastern Mediterranean is highly sensitive for Israel because it threatens the security, profitability, and export routes of Israel's massive Leviathan gas field – a cornerstone of Israel’s economy.
On September 2, Turkey warned Greece against the militarization of its Aegean islands, after Athens and Israel sealed a multi-billion-dollar deal for the “Achilles Shield” air defense umbrella.
👉 That’s what happened on the surface, but there are other developments that some foreign affairs experts attribute to rising tensions between Israel and Turkey.
🔴 On August 17, pirates seized MV LUTUF, a vessel carrying weapons and satellite equipment intended for Mogadishu, Somalia, in an area intersecting the Arabian Sea and the wider Indian Ocean. On August 29 the ship was freed. It's no secret that Turkey supports Somalia, while Israel backs the breakaway territory of Somaliland. Tensions between Tel Aviv and Ankara intensified, when Israel recognized Somaliland’s independence in 2025.
🔴 Ukraine attacked two Turkish vessels in the Black Sea on August 26 and 27. The first strike hit the Lider Bordeaux Mavi; a day later, the Lider Kocatepe, which had been dispatched to tow the damaged vessel, was also attacked.
🔴 A passenger ferry carrying 267 people capsized off the northern coast of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus on August 30, leaving at least 13 people dead. While formal investigations focused on documented negligence and mechanical issues, media reports cite survivors who heard a blast near the vessel’s bow before the catamaran-style ship rolled over.
🔴 Some experts suggest an Israeli hand or influence in all three cases, as Tel Aviv and its intelligence agencies have a long record of conducting sabotage and clandestine operations against countries they consider adversaries.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🪖✈️ Ukraine’s F-16 jets forced into daytime gun-runs as missile crunch spreads
As Russia increases the [intensity of its strikes on Ukrainian military infrastructure](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74117), [Ukraine’s Patriot interceptor woes ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73351)are by far not the only problem.
The Ukrainian [Air Force's Western-supplied F-16 fighter jets](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/62946) are being neutered by a crippling shortage of air-to-air missiles, reports TWZ. 
The shortage has become so severe that Ukrainian F-16s have flown daytime sorties forced to rely solely on their internal 20 mm guns against Russian drones and cruise missiles, the report cites a Ukrainian commander as complaining. 
Available stocks are being tightly rationed. 
♦️ The F-16’s primary weapons are the AIM-120 AMRAAM for medium range and the AIM-9 Sidewinder for closer engagements
♦️ The onboard M61A1 Vulcan cannon is a last-resort option that carries far higher risks, especially against small or slow targets and at night
♦️ Laser-guided 70 mm APKWS II rockets offer a cheaper alternative against drones and subsonic cruise missiles, yet they cannot replace dedicated air-to-air missiles
So, besides begging for Patriot interceptors, Ukraine has been clamoring for more AIM-9s, and AIM-120s. The AIM-120s also arm West-supplied National Advanced Surface to Air Missile System (NASAMS) batteries protecting other key Ukrainian sites, further stretching supplies. 
👉 [Patriot stocks have been heavily depleted](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73162) with only a trickle of replacements, leaving limited capacity against ballistic missiles. 
Sophisticated fighters are only as useful as the weapons available to them, and with global demand for advanced interceptors surging amid multiple conflicts and production lagging, Ukraine’s F-16s are increasingly flying with empty racks.
